title: Will Thanksgiving Dinner Cost More This Year?
summary: If your family is cooking Thanksgiving dinner this year, the grocery bill might be a surprise. Grocery costs have risen nearly 22 percent over the past five years, pushed up by wars, tariffs, and severe weather. Still, experts say it is not clear whether your Thanksgiving meal will cost more than last year's. Two groups came to different answers. The American Farm Bureau Federation says the cost will be up more than 6 percent compared with last year, led by cranberries and dinner rolls. The Wells Fargo Agri-Food Institute found something different: drinks cost more now, but the average food bill will be a little cheaper than last year, thanks in part to sales. Wells Fargo economist Michael Swanson warned that a cheap turkey is not the whole story — shoppers can still spend too much on the rest of the food. A LendingTree survey found that 53 percent of people said inflation was changing their holiday plans or spending. Andre Andrews said prices are 'too high,' but he still plans to smoke a turkey and a roast.
why_it_matters: If food costs more, your family may have to change what it buys or cooks for the holidays.
